name: Plank shin guards
description: Two split lengths of plank, padded with rags and tied on over the shins with string.
notes: A pair laid flat side by side: each guard is a split pine plank 260 mm long, 80 mm wide and 15 mm thick with a splintered end, a rag pad wrapped round it near each end and string lashed twice round each pad, the loose ends hanging off the outer edge. The planks guard only the shins, so it takes the `shins` slot the splint greaves use. Protection and wear are guesses for thin softwood. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel light leg guards
description: A pair of forged leg guards in mild steel. A narrow plate rides down each thigh and another down each shin, on chain legs left bare at the knee.
notes: The model's root: plates in `steel-bright`. A pair of guards 600 mm long laid side by side, convex side up, each a chain leg from hip to ankle with a narrow plate 120 degrees round down the thigh and another down the shin, bare chain showing at the knee and ankle, held on by two buckled leather straps; the chain is `steel-mail-dark` so it reads apart from the plates. The two half-round guards lie open side down at full length and enclose air inside the box. The xl size shares the model. `legs` is the trousers' slot and plate goes on over them, so it takes `shins`, as the full-length splint leg guards do; a slot for whole-leg armour over trousers is open. Wearing one guard on one leg has no content field. Protection follows the steel arm guards of the same weight and steel. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
